q: BCO 1-7 says the presbyterian form of government is
o: essential to the existence of a true church
necessary to the perfection of the church's order, but not essential to its existence
one arrangement among many, with no scriptural warrant
w: The claim is strong about order and deliberately limited about existence, which is why 2-2 can recognise other bodies as true branches.
title: Christ, the King and Head

q: According to the Preface, what did Christ give his church?
w: The Preface lists officers, oracles and ordinances, along with a system of doctrine, government, discipline and worship.
title: Christ, the King and Head

q: Calling church power ministerial and declarative means that a church court
o: may make new laws binding the conscience
declares and applies the law of Christ found in Scripture
may overrule Scripture in hard cases
has no real authority at all
w: Courts may frame symbols of faith, testify against error and decide cases of conscience, but they can make no laws binding the conscience.
title: Christ, the King and Head

q: The sharpest structural difference between presbyterian and congregational government is
o: whether the congregation elects its officers
whether a lower court is subject to review and control by a higher court
whether the pastor preaches every week
w: Congregational churches elect officers too. The dividing line is that in presbyterian government the courts are connected and reviewable.
title: Who Runs the Church

q: Against episcopal government, the book holds that
o: bishops are a higher order than presbyters
bishop, pastor and elder name one office
w: BCO 8-1 says these titles describe the various duties of one office and do not indicate grades.
title: Who Runs the Church

q: In the PCA text of the Confession, the civil magistrate may
o: administer the sacraments in an emergency
protect the church without preferring one denomination over another
appoint elders in a vacant church
w: The American revision removed the magistrate from ecclesiastical matters and left him the duty of protection without preference.
title: Who Runs the Church

q: A church has a pastor and one ruling elder. The ruling elder alone
o: is a Session with the pastor absent
does not constitute a Session, but takes spiritual oversight and reports to presbytery
w: With one ruling elder and no pastor there is no Session. He is to give oversight, represent the church at presbytery, grant letters and report matters needing a court.
title: The Marks of Presbyterian Government

q: Which sentence states the connectional principle?
o: Each court is independent within its sphere
Every act of jurisdiction is the act of the whole church performed through the appropriate organ
Higher courts may not review lower courts
Only the General Assembly exercises jurisdiction
w: BCO 11-4 denies that the courts are separate and independent tribunals.
title: The Marks of Presbyterian Government

q: The power exercised by the people, according to BCO 3-1, extends to
o: the choice of officers Christ has appointed
w: Power vests in the whole body, and the people’s part in it is the choice of officers.
title: The Marks of Presbyterian Government

q: The first General Assembly of the church now called the PCA met
o: at Briarwood Presbyterian Church, Birmingham, in December 1973
w: It met December 4 to 7, 1973, and the second Assembly met at Macon in September 1974, where the present name was taken.
title: How This Book Came To Be

q: The 1788 American revision of the Confession touched
o: the civil magistrate's place in church matters
w: Chapters 20.4, 23.3 and 31.2 were revised, which removed the state from ecclesiastical matters.
title: How This Book Came To Be

q: Which body joined the PCA in 1982?
o: The Reformed Presbyterian Church, Evangelical Synod
w: The RPCES joined in 1982.
title: How This Book Came To Be

q: Why does the book connect the ruling elder to the elders of Israel?
o: Because the New Testament never mentions elders
Because the visible church is one and the same in every age, and Christ has furnished men besides ministers with gifts to govern
Because the office is a modern invention
w: BCO 8-9 draws the line from elders of the people under the law to ruling elders in the gospel church, and 2-1 keeps the visible church one across the ages.
title: A People Taught and Judged

q: In Exodus 18 and Deuteronomy 1, the hardest cases are
w: Shared judgment with a route upward for hard cases is the pattern later called graded courts.
title: A People Taught and Judged

q: BCO 31-5 requires that a person wronged
o: try the means of reconciliation Christ requires before becoming a prosecutor
forgive and never mention the matter
take the case straight to presbytery
w: A court may still investigate a personal offense as if general when the interest of religion demands it, but the injured party must first take the steps of Matthew 18.
title: The Shepherd Who Rules

q: The Confession locates the keys of the kingdom in
o: the apostles only, and no successors
w: WCF 30.2 commits the keys to church officers, who shut and open the kingdom by the Word and censures.
title: The Shepherd Who Rules

q: The Confession cites Acts 15 in support of
o: assemblies commonly called synods or councils
the office of bishop over presbyters
w: WCF 31.1 rests the case for such assemblies on the pattern of Acts 15, with its proof texts drawn from that chapter.
title: Churches Learning to Decide

q: According to WCF 31.4, synods and councils are to
o: decide civil matters when the state asks for help only
handle nothing but what is ecclesiastical, apart from humble petition in extraordinary cases or advice when required by the magistrate
advise on any public question they choose
stay silent on immorality outside the church
w: This is the confessional root of what is often called the spirituality of the church, and it stands behind BCO 11-1.
title: Churches Learning to Decide

q: 1 Timothy 4:14 speaks of a gift given with the laying on of hands of
w: Ordination in this book is ordinarily the act of a court, with prayer and the laying on of hands.
title: Churches Learning to Decide

q: Which principle holds that a church may set its own terms of admission, and may err in doing so without infringing anyone else’s liberty?
w: Principle 2 grants the liberty and names the misuse of it in the same breath.
title: The Preliminary Principles

q: The principle that no judicatory may make laws binding the conscience is
w: Principle 7 states that all church power is only ministerial and declarative.
title: The Preliminary Principles

q: Principle 8 explains why church discipline
o: carries civil penalties in some states
has force only from its justice, public approval and Christ's blessing
requires the consent of the magistrate
w: Discipline is purely moral or spiritual and is attended with no civil effects.
title: The Preliminary Principles

q: Which of these is part of the Constitution?
o: Appendix J, the sample terms of call
w: The Constitution is the Confession and Catechisms with the Book of Church Order. Appendices and Assembly rules are printed alongside it.
title: What the Constitution Is

q: Which parts of the Directory for Worship carry full constitutional authority?
w: The rest is an approved guide, taken seriously as the mind of the church but without the force of law.
title: What the Constitution Is

q: A judicial decision of the Assembly
o: binds only the parties and may be cited later as to the principle decided
binds every session in every future case absolutely
has no weight beyond the case
may be set aside by a session at will
w: BCO 14-7 states both the binding effect on the parties and the use of decided principles in later similar cases.
title: What the Constitution Is

q: Suspending a member from the Lord’s Table is an exercise of
o: the power of order by the pastor
the power of jurisdiction by a court
the deacons' authority over the elements
w: Jurisdiction is a joint power exercised by presbyters in courts, never severally.
title: Church Power and Its Limits

q: BCO 11-2 says church courts may establish rules for government and worship, provided that
o: a majority of the congregation agrees
they agree with the doctrines of Scripture, with only circumstantial details left to prudence
w: The Confession says the same thing about circumstances common to human societies.
title: Church Power and Its Limits

q: Which statement is true of church courts under BCO 11-1?
o: They may impose fines in serious cases
They have jurisdiction in civil disputes between members
Their authority is in all respects moral or spiritual
They may call on the magistrate to enforce censures
w: They have no power to inflict temporal pains and penalties.
title: Church Power and Its Limits

q: A presbytery may grant an exception to a stated difference only if
o: the candidate promises never to teach it
the difference is neither hostile to the system nor strikes at the vitals of religion
three quarters of the presbytery agree
the difference concerns worship rather than doctrine
w: That is the test in 21-4 for ordination and in 19-2 for licensure.
title: Vows, Subscription and Stated Differences

q: Which finding is not one of the four recorded in presbytery minutes?
o: More than semantic but not out of accord
w: The fourth recorded finding is that the difference is out of accord, that is hostile to the system or striking at the vitals of religion.
title: Vows, Subscription and Stated Differences

q: If a minister’s views change after ordination, the vow requires him to
o: make the change known to his presbytery on his own initiative
w: The second ordination question contains that promise.
title: Vows, Subscription and Stated Differences

q: Where is the jurisdiction of a particular church lodged?
w: Jurisdiction is a joint power and is lodged in the Session, which consists of the pastor, associate pastors and ruling elders.
title: The Visible Church and the Particular Church

q: According to BCO 2-2, other denominations are to be recognised as true branches of the church
o: if they maintain the Word and Sacraments in their fundamental integrity
if they are older than the PCA
w: That test also matters in discipline, at 38-3, when a member joins another body.
title: The Visible Church and the Particular Church

q: A mission church differs from a particular church chiefly in that
o: its members are not PCA members
it has no permanent governing body and is supervised by others
it may not celebrate the Sacraments
w: Its goal is organisation as a particular church as soon as this can be done decently and in good order.
title: The Visible Church and the Particular Church

q: Children of believers are
o: members of the church by covenant and birth
candidates for membership only after profession
members of no church until baptized as adults
w: BCO 6-1 makes them non-communing members, entitled to baptism, oversight, instruction and government.
title: Members: Children and Communicants

q: Who judges when a covenant child may be admitted to the Lord’s Table?
w: No age is fixed; the judgment is left to the prudence of the Session.
title: Members: Children and Communicants

q: An associate member may not
o: vote in a congregational meeting or hold office
w: Associate membership is for believers temporarily away from their permanent homes, who keep membership in their home churches.
title: Members: Children and Communicants

q: A member moves away, is advised of his duty, and does nothing for a year. The Session
o: leaves the name on the roll indefinitely
w: Special cases such as servicemen and students are excepted.
title: Transfers, Withdrawal and Erasure

q: A member in good standing joins an evangelical church of another denomination. The Session should
o: record the irregularity, acknowledge the new membership and remove the name
w: Erasure with warning is for joining a body judged not to maintain the Word and Sacraments in their fundamental integrity.
title: Transfers, Withdrawal and Erasure

q: A member warned under 38-4 asks in writing for process. The Session
w: The Session may also institute process on its own if the offense requires it.
title: Transfers, Withdrawal and Erasure

q: The ordinary and perpetual classes of office are
o: elder and deacon, with two orders of elder
w: BCO 7-2 sets two classes and places teaching and ruling elders as two orders within the class of elder.
title: Offices: Elders and Deacons

q: Assistants appointed under 9-7 are
o: not officers and not subjects for ordination
w: They assist the deacons in caring for those in need, under the Session’s appointment.
title: Offices: Elders and Deacons

q: BCO 7-1 teaches that extraordinary officers
o: have no successors, since revelation was completed
continue only on the mission field
w: Their gifts were tied to the completion of revelation at the close of the apostolic age.
title: Offices: Elders and Deacons

q: A teaching elder commissioned as an evangelist under 8-6 is commissioned for
o: a renewable term of twelve months
as long as the mission church exists
w: By separate actions presbytery may add power to examine, ordain and install officers and to organise churches.
title: The Elder

q: Which duty belongs to the order of teaching elder rather than to elders generally?
w: Preaching, reading and expounding the Word and administering the Sacraments are added to what he shares with all elders.
title: The Elder

q: BCO 16-4 requires officers to affirm
o: the sinfulness of fallen desires and the hope of progressive sanctification
that temptation is not sin in any sense
that sanctification is complete at conversion
w: It also requires commitment to Spirit-empowered victory over sinful temptations, inclinations and actions.
title: The Elder

q: Deacons may take final action on a matter of special importance affecting church property
o: only with Session approval and the consent of the congregation
w: BCO 9-2 requires both, and 12-5 gives the Session power to approve actions of special importance affecting property.
title: The Deacon

q: How often must the Board of Deacons meet separately?
o: At least once a quarter, and whenever the Session requests
w: A joint quarterly meeting with the Session is also desirable.
title: The Deacon

q: If a church cannot secure deacons,
o: the duties of the office fall to the ruling elders
w: The same rule appears when a church is organised without deacons.
title: The Deacon

q: The three marks of an ordinary call to office are
o: inward testimony of conscience, approbation of God's people, and the judgment of a lawful court
inward call, seminary degree and a congregation's vote
a pastor's recommendation, an examination and a majority vote
w: BCO 16-1 holds all three together as the calling of God by the Spirit.
title: Calling and Ordination

q: No man may be ordained except
o: to the performance of a definite work
with the consent of presbytery and synod
w: Every ecclesiastical office, according to the Scriptures, is a special charge.
title: Calling and Ordination

q: A ruling elder released from active duties is later elected again by the same church. He is
w: Ordination to these offices is perpetual, so it is not repeated.
title: Calling and Ordination

q: How much notice must a congregation receive before a meeting to elect officers?
w: One week is the general notice for congregational meetings; elections of officers require thirty days.
title: Electing Ruling Elders and Deacons

q: A congregation votes to ask the Session to release an officer, and the Session neither reports nor acts for sixty days. Members may
o: file a complaint against the Session
w: The same remedy applies where the Session reports that it declined to dissolve the relationship.
title: Electing Ruling Elders and Deacons

q: An officer designated emeritus
o: keeps his vote at Session meetings
may attend and take part in discussion, but may not vote
w: An editorial comment preserves the vote for those granted emeritus status before June 22, 1984.
title: Electing Ruling Elders and Deacons

q: A ruling elder who sat on the Session whose action is complained against comes to presbytery. He
o: may sit and vote on the complaint
may not vote on the complaint
votes only if the Session asks him to
w: Members of a lower court keep their seat above except in cases of appeal or complaint.
title: The Courts and Their Jurisdiction

q: The courts of the PCA are
o: Session, presbytery and the General Assembly
w: All three are presbyteries in nature, since each is made up only of presbyters.
title: The Courts and Their Jurisdiction

q: Extracts from a court’s records, signed by the clerk,
o: are evidence in any ecclesiastical court
may be granted only to members
w: The clerk preserves the records and grants extracts whenever properly required.
title: The Courts and Their Jurisdiction

q: A church has a pastor and five ruling elders. What is the quorum of its Session?
o: The pastor and one ruling elder
The pastor and two ruling elders
w: With four or more ruling elders the quorum is the pastor and two ruling elders, unless the Session has fixed a larger one.
title: The Session

q: Two ruling elders ask the pastor to convene the Session. He
o: may decline if he judges it unnecessary
must wait for the next stated meeting
w: The pastor has power to convene the Session when he judges it requisite, and shall always convene it when requested by any two ruling elders.
title: The Session

q: Which of these does the Session not do?
o: Examine, ordain and install ruling elders and deacons on their election
Control the music in public worship
w: Ordaining ministers belongs to presbytery.
title: The Session

q: A congregation has 800 communing members. How many ruling elder representatives may it send to presbytery?
w: Two cover the first 350. The remaining 450 are a fraction of 500 and add one more, giving three. The same formula sets representation at the General Assembly.
title: The Presbytery

q: What is the quorum of a presbytery?
o: Three ministers with at least three ruling elders
w: A presbytery may fix a larger quorum for itself by majority vote at a stated meeting.
title: The Presbytery

q: A Session is unable to exercise its authority in a matter. Presbytery
w: This power sits in the opening sentence of 13-9, and there are related routes in 33-1 and 40-5.
title: The Presbytery

q: Which body’s report comes directly to the floor rather than through a committee of commissioners?
w: So do the Committee on Constitutional Business, the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, the Nominating Committee and ad interim committees.
title: The General Assembly

q: The quorum of the General Assembly is
o: one hundred commissioners, half teaching and half ruling elders, from at least a third of the presbyteries
w: A special meeting has its own requirements in 14-3.
title: The General Assembly

q: Receiving another denomination under the Assembly’s jurisdiction requires
o: a majority of the Assembly only
the consent of three-fourths of the presbyteries
w: Full organic union is governed separately by 26-5, which requires three-fourths at each of three steps.
title: The General Assembly

q: The difference between a committee and a commission is that a commission
o: may conclude the business referred to it
w: A committee examines, considers and reports; a commission deliberates and concludes.
title: Commissions and the Standing Judicial Commission

q: A presbytery commission clothed with judicial powers must have a quorum of at least
o: two teaching elders and two ruling elders
one more than half, whatever the makeup
w: The general rule of one more than half applies to other commissions unless presbytery decides otherwise.
title: Commissions and the Standing Judicial Commission

q: A decision of the Standing Judicial Commission is
o: the final decision of the Assembly, apart from the minority procedure
subject to appeal by any member
w: The Assembly may direct a retrial if exceptions are taken when its minutes are reviewed.
title: Commissions and the Standing Judicial Commission

q: In the Assembly’s Overtures Committee, the previous question is adopted by
o: two thirds of those present and voting
three-fourths of the members present and voting
w: That committee is also barred from motions to limit or extend the limits of debate.
title: How a Court Does Business

q: An amendment must be
o: germane to the motion it alters
submitted in writing a day in advance
w: The Assembly’s rules define germane by reference to the standard manual.
title: How a Court Does Business

q: When a rule of order conflicts with a requirement of the Book of Church Order,
o: the court may suspend the book by two thirds
the matter goes to the Assembly
w: Parliamentary rules order the business; the Constitution sets what the business may conclude.
title: How a Court Does Business

q: Who may join in a protest?
o: Only those who had a right to vote on the question
Any member of the higher court
w: A member who could not vote on an appeal or complaint may have an objection recorded instead.
title: The Rights of the Minority

q: A dissent, protest or objection must be filed
o: within thirty days following the meeting, or before the Assembly adjourns
w: Filing is with the clerk of the lower court, or with the Assembly’s clerk before adjournment.
title: The Rights of the Minority

q: Which action can suspend a decision while a complaint is pending?
o: A vote of a third of the members present when the action was taken
w: Notice of complaint by itself does not suspend the action complained against.
title: The Rights of the Minority

q: Why do the Assembly’s guidelines want points of order and appeals from the chair recorded?
o: For the sake of any case carried to a higher court, and for the protection of a minority
Because Robert's Rules require verbatim minutes
w: The reason given is the later case and the minority, which is why the guideline asks for the chair’s stated reason as well as the ruling.
title: The Chair, the Record and the Minority

q: A member believes the moderator has ruled wrongly. His recourse is
o: a complaint to presbytery at once
an appeal from the decision of the chair, decided by the body
a protest, which ends the matter
w: A complaint lies against an act of the court, and has its own sixty-day period. The immediate remedy in the room is the appeal from the chair.
title: The Chair, the Record and the Minority

q: Under the Assembly’s committee rules, a chairman who wants to argue for a motion must
o: ask the moderator of the Assembly
w: He also ordinarily does not vote on a question.
title: The Chair, the Record and the Minority

q: How long must an applicant have been a member of the endorsing congregation?
w: Presbytery may deem a case extraordinary and receive him sooner.
title: Candidates and Licensure

q: A man may be taken under care and examined for ordination at the same presbytery meeting.
o: True, if his gifts are evident
False, because at least a year of internship must intervene
False, unless he transfers from another denomination
w: He may, however, be taken under care, licensed and made an intern at one meeting.
title: Candidates and Licensure

q: A licence to preach
o: expires after four years and may be renewed
expires when the man is ordained elsewhere only
lasts until the next stated meeting
w: It may also be terminated at any time by a simple majority with reasons recorded.
title: Candidates and Licensure

q: An intern serving a church may
o: vote in Session as an intern
moderate the Session in his own right
w: He may chair a Session meeting temporarily at the moderator’s request, under supervision, but he is not a member and does not vote.
title: Internship and the Call

q: A proper call must include
o: financial arrangements and an assurance of liberty to preach the whole counsel of God
w: It must be written and in presbytery’s hands before presbytery acts on it.
title: Internship and the Call

q: Who may vote in the election of a pastor?
o: All communing members in good and regular standing
w: A majority of votes cast, excluding blanks and abstentions, elects.
title: Internship and the Call

q: Omitting a part of the trials for ordination requires
o: three-fourths approval of presbytery, with reasons recorded
w: The same threshold covers omission of the educational requirements.
title: Ordination Trials and Installation

q: Which is not among the trials listed in 21-4?
o: A thesis on an assigned theological topic
An exegesis using the original languages
A written examination in church history
A public examination by the congregation
w: The congregation elects and answers its own questions at the service, but the trials belong to presbytery.
title: Ordination Trials and Installation

q: In the ordination of an assistant pastor
o: only questions one to seven are used, and the Session is addressed
w: The eighth question concerns taking charge of the congregation that called him.
title: Ordination Trials and Installation

q: Who calls an assistant pastor?
o: The Session, with presbytery's permission and approval
w: Because he is not elected by the congregation, he is not a member of the Session.
title: Pastoral Relations and Their End

q: An associate pastor succeeding the senior pastor without an intervening field of labour requires
o: four-fifths of the congregation by secret ballot and three-fourths of presbytery
w: Presbytery must also weigh whether the earlier dissolution was brought about in Christian love and good order.
title: Pastoral Relations and Their End

q: A stated supply relation may run for
o: no longer than one year, renewable
as long as the Session wishes
w: Student supply and ruling elder supply are on the same footing.
title: Pastoral Relations and Their End

q: A church has 260 communing members. What proportion must sign a written request to force the Session to call a meeting?
w: A fifth applies to churches of more than 100 and not more than 300.
title: Congregational Meetings

q: The Session receives a proper request and does nothing for thirty days. Members may
w: Complaint is the standing remedy against an act or failure of a court.
title: Congregational Meetings

q: The quorum of a congregational meeting in a church of 400 resident communing members is
w: A fourth is the quorum only in churches of not more than 100 resident communing members.
title: Congregational Meetings

q: Under BCO 25-9, a congregation’s property is
o: held in trust for the presbytery
held in trust for the General Assembly
owned by the congregation, with no right of reversion to any court
owned jointly by the church and the presbytery
w: Chapter 25 is also framed as a solemn covenant that the church will never try to take a congregation’s property against its will.
title: Property and the Freedom to Withdraw

q: How much notice must a congregation have before voting to withdraw from the PCA?
w: The relationship is voluntary and may be ended for reasons that seem sufficient to the congregation.
title: Property and the Freedom to Withdraw

q: In the PC(USA), a congregation’s relationship to the denomination can be severed
o: only by constitutional action of the presbytery
w: Its property is held in trust for the denomination under G-4.0203.
title: Property and the Freedom to Withdraw

q: A mission church is governed
o: by a temporary system of government provided by presbytery
w: The options are an evangelist, a mother church Session, or a commission serving as a temporary Session.
title: Planting and Organizing a Church

q: A new church can be organised
o: by the members petitioning a Session
only by the authority of presbytery
by the Assembly's committee in all cases
w: Presbytery approves the petition, appoints an organizing commission and sets the service.
title: Planting and Organizing a Church

q: If deacons are not elected when a church is organised,
o: their duties fall to the Session until deacons can be secured
w: The same rule appears in chapter 9 for any church that cannot secure deacons.
title: Planting and Organizing a Church

q: The two senses of discipline in BCO 27-1 are
o: the whole government and training of the church, and judicial process
w: Most of what a Session does day by day is discipline in the first sense.
title: What Discipline Is For

q: Which is not named among the ends of judicial discipline?
o: The vindication of the honour of Christ
The punishment of the offender for its own sake
The spiritual good of offenders themselves
w: The power is given for building up, not for destruction.
title: What Discipline Is For

q: BCO 27-5 requires that the scriptural steps
o: be used at the court's discretion
w: The steps run from instruction, through private admonition and witnesses, to the action of the court.
title: What Discipline Is For

q: Which censure is never definite in duration?
w: The book says plainly that there is no definite suspension from the Sacraments.
title: Offenses and Censures

q: Excommunication is reserved for
o: gross crime or heresy where the offender is incorrigible and contumacious
w: Its design is to reclaim the offender, to deliver the church from scandal, and to inspire fear by the example.
title: Offenses and Censures

q: An offense may be charged only if it
o: offends a majority of the Session
can be proved contrary to the Word of God as interpreted in the standards
w: BCO 29-1 closes the door on charges that rest on preference rather than Scripture.
title: Offenses and Censures

q: At the first meeting after a charge is laid, the court may, without consent of parties,
o: appoint a prosecutor, order the indictment drawn and served, and cite the accused
w: The citation must give at least ten days before the next meeting.
title: Parties, Charges and Trial

q: Who is always the accuser in a case of process?
w: The prosecutor is the church’s representative and has all its rights in the case.
title: Parties, Charges and Trial

q: May an attorney represent an accused person as professional counsel?
o: No, though the accused may be represented by a qualified member of this church
w: A member of the court who serves as representative may not sit in judgment in the case.
title: Parties, Charges and Trial

q: The administrative suspension of a court member under process requires
o: a majority of the commission trying the case
two-thirds of the members present and voting at the Session or presbytery
w: It is never done by way of censure, and the 2026 amendment made clear that the two-thirds vote belongs to the court even where a commission conducts the process.
title: Parties, Charges and Trial

q: A Session refuses to act in a case of public scandal. Presbytery must assume jurisdiction if
o: two other Sessions of churches in the same presbytery request it
w: The parallel provision at the Assembly level requires the request of two other presbyteries.
title: Members, Ministers and Evidence

q: Divesting a minister of office without censure under 34-10 requires
w: He must receive written notice stating the grounds, be heard in his own defense, and may appeal.
title: Members, Ministers and Evidence

q: A charge is established by
o: more than one witness, or one witness with corroborative evidence
w: It belongs to the court to judge the degree of credibility due to all evidence.
title: Members, Ministers and Evidence

q: Under the 2026 provision, raising an indefinite suspension to deposition or excommunication requires
o: a new trial from the beginning
thirty days notice and a hearing before the court having jurisdiction
w: The hearing is before the court itself, not a trial commission, and the person may then appeal.
title: Censure, Restoration and Cases Without Process

q: In a case without process, the written confession must be
o: approved by the accused and by the court before judgment
w: It is co-signed and appended to the minutes, and no other information may be presented without written consent.
title: Censure, Restoration and Cases Without Process

q: A minister satisfied that God has not called him to the ministry may be divested without censure
o: at the same meeting he reports it
at the next stated meeting, if presbytery concurs after full deliberation
w: This is 38-2, a voluntary route, distinct from the involuntary divestiture of 34-10.
title: Censure, Restoration and Cases Without Process

q: How often are the records of a lower court reviewed?
o: Only when a complaint is filed
At the discretion of the higher court
w: Where records are not presented, the higher court may require them immediately.
title: How Higher Courts Review Lower Courts

q: Under the standards of review, a higher court owes no special deference when the issue is
w: On facts and on matters of discretion the standard is clear error.
title: How Higher Courts Review Lower Courts

q: A judgment in a judicial case may be reversed
w: Once notice of appeal or complaint is given, the judicial proceedings are not dealt with under review and control.
title: How Higher Courts Review Lower Courts

q: A member disagrees with his Session’s decision to sell part of the church property. His remedy is
w: Appeal belongs to a party against whom judgment was rendered in a judicial case.
title: References, Appeals and Complaints

q: A complaint must first be filed with
o: the court whose act is alleged to be in error, within sixty days
w: If it is denied, notice goes to both clerks within thirty days of notification.
title: References, Appeals and Complaints

q: Notice of appeal has the effect of
o: suspending the judgment until the case is decided
nothing until the higher court accepts it
w: The court of original jurisdiction may still restrict the appellant by a two-thirds vote, never as censure.
title: References, Appeals and Complaints

q: Which route begins with the lower court itself asking for help before deciding?
w: A reference may ask for advice, or for the higher court to take the case, or for extra elders to sit with the lower court.
title: References, Appeals and Complaints

q: Which parts of the Directory for Worship have the force of law?
w: The rest is an approved guide, taken seriously as the mind of the church.
title: Principles of Worship and the Lord’s Day

q: Who decides who may preach in a congregation?
w: The Session also ensures the Word is preached only by men sufficiently qualified.
title: Principles of Worship and the Lord’s Day

q: According to BCO 50-3, Scripture in public worship is to be read
o: from a paraphrase when it is clearer
from a good translation, not a paraphrase, in the language of the people
w: Reading by the minister is distinguished from responsive reading, in which the people give expression to contrition, adoration and gratitude.
title: Principles of Worship and the Lord’s Day

q: Who determines how often the Lord’s Supper is observed?
w: The book requires frequent observance and leaves the stated times to the Session as it judges most for edification.
title: Baptism, Profession and the Lord’s Supper

q: Baptism is to be administered
o: in the presence of the congregation, under the supervision of the Session
by any believing parent in an emergency
only at a stated service of the Assembly
w: It is not to be administered by any private person, but by a minister of Christ.
title: Baptism, Profession and the Lord’s Supper

q: The invitation to the Lord’s Table in 58-4 may be
o: only to members of the congregation
only to those the Session has approved in advance
either to communicants in good standing in any evangelical church who profess the true religion, or to those the Session has approved
left to each person's conscience without direction
w: The choice between the two forms belongs to the Session.
title: Baptism, Profession and the Lord’s Supper

q: Which section of chapter 59 carries full constitutional authority?
w: It restricts ministers of this church to solemnizing marriages between one man and one woman.
title: Marriage, the Sick, Burial and the Home

q: A general day of fasting or thanksgiving for the whole church is called by
w: Sessions determine for congregations and presbyteries for larger districts.
title: Marriage, the Sick, Burial and the Home

q: The proper object of a funeral service is
o: the worship of God and the consolation of the living
instruction in the doctrine of the last things
w: The service is otherwise left largely to the minister’s discretion.
title: Marriage, the Sick, Burial and the Home

q: Amending the Book of Church Order requires
o: an Assembly majority, two-thirds of presbyteries, and a majority of the next Assembly
w: Three-fourths at every stage is the rule for the Confession and Catechisms.
title: How the Constitution Changes

q: May a presbytery approve part of an amendment and reject the rest?
o: Only as the Assembly that recommended it directs
Yes, if it records its reasons
w: BCO 26-4 forbids dividing the parts otherwise.
title: How the Constitution Changes

q: An overture is ordinarily
o: a letter from an individual member
the request of a presbytery for action by the Assembly
a report of a permanent committee
w: Communications from individuals are received only where they have no other access to the Assembly.
title: How the Constitution Changes

q: The 2026 amendment to 31-10 requires
o: two-thirds of members present and voting at the Session or presbytery, even where a commission conducts the process
presbytery approval in every Session case
w: The suspension is administrative and is never imposed as a censure.
title: What Changed Lately

q: Which section was added in 2026?
w: It allows an indefinite suspension to be raised without new process, with notice, a hearing and a right of appeal.
title: What Changed Lately

q: Since 2025, a complaint filed after judicial process has begun is
o: held until the judicial case, and any appeal, is finished
w: During the process the accused may still raise objections under 32-14, and those decisions may be reviewable on appeal.
title: What Changed Lately

q: Which court exists in the PC(USA) but not in the PCA?
w: The PCA’s courts are Session, presbytery and Assembly.
title: Beside Other Presbyterian Churches

q: The PCA General Assembly differs from the OPC assembly in that
o: every teaching elder in good standing may sit, rather than a fixed number of commissioners elected by presbyteries
it is a court of first instance
w: The OPC assembly is delegated, with about 150 voting commissioners.
title: Beside Other Presbyterian Churches

q: A congregation wishing to leave its denomination with its property has the clearest path in
o: the PC(USA), under the trust clause
w: In the PC(USA) the property is held in trust and severance requires presbytery action.
title: Beside Other Presbyterian Churches
